subject: Decision log + handoff: runtime outputs, streaming & tool-calling
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@cartehealth.com>
Cc: Danielle Cho <danielle.cho@cartehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Apr 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Decision log + handoff: runtime outputs, streaming & tool-calling

Hi Elena / Danielle,

Thanks for the productive call this morning. Per our discussion I captured the key decisions and open items so engineering and CS can start the implementation plan: 

Decisions agreed:
- Use streaming API for live transcription + partial results (low-latency path).
- Tool-calling contract: Redwood will expose two tool endpoints for Carte: `patient_lookup` (sync) and `order_submit` (async w/ callback).
- Structured output: JSON schema v1 will enumerate `events[]` with typed fields (id, ts, intent, entities, tools_called).

Open items / action owners:
- Redwood: provide canonical JSON schema (deliver v1 by Mon 4/14) — Priyom + Camila (attachment: carte-schema-proposal-v1.json).
- Carte: confirm required fields for `patient_lookup` (patient_id or ssn?) and SLA for `order_submit` callback. — Elena
- Both: finalize SLOs for streaming (p50 < 200ms token, p95 < 700ms) and batching window for peak load.

Attached: implementation checklist and initial schema draft. Next steps I propose:
1) Camila to run a brief dev sync Tues 4/15 (30m) to walk schema and tool contract.
2) Monica to create CS acceptance criteria and success metrics.
3) Exchange a signed SOW/DocuSign to kick off sprint 0.

Elena — can you confirm the `patient_lookup` inputs by EOD Monday? If you want, we can accept a short form (CSV) of the fields.

Thanks,

--
Priyom Das
Solutions PM, Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0192

Attachments: RD-98542_implementation-checklist.xlsx, carte-schema-proposal-v1.json
From: Elena Morales <elena@cartehealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: Danielle Cho <danielle.cho@cartehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Apr 2025 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Decision log + handoff: runtime outputs, streaming & tool-calling

Thanks Priyom — this is great and mirrors our notes. Quick clarifications: 

- Patient lookup fields: we can provide `patient_id` (recommended) and `dob`. SSN is sensitive; avoid if possible. If Redwood needs a stronger identifier for matching, we can discuss a hashed id approach.
- `order_submit` SLA: we need confirmation that callbacks will be delivered within 30s under normal load; if not possible, we need a retry/backoff pattern documented.

We reviewed the attached schema and had two requests: 
1) Add an optional `confidence` field on top-level events.
2) Make `tools_called` an array of objects with `tool_name`, `status`, `request_id` to aid reconciliation.

We can meet Tue 4/15 11:00-11:30 PT for the dev sync. Danielle will bring our platform engineer.

Thanks,

Elena

--
Elena Morales
Head of Product Integrations, Carte Health
elena@cartehealth.com
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@cartehealth.com>, Danielle Cho <danielle.cho@cartehealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Apr 2025 08:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Decision log + handoff: runtime outputs, streaming & tool-calling

Great — thanks for the notes, Elena. Quick technical response ahead of today's sync.

Summary of what Redwood will provide in Sprint 0 (deliverables and acceptance criteria):
- Schema deliverable: `carte-schema-proposal-v1.json` (we'll add `confidence` and convert `tools_called` -> array of objects).
- Tool contract: OpenAPI-ish spec for `patient_lookup` (sync) and `order_submit` (async callback). We'll include sample payloads and error codes.
- Streaming SLOs: we can meet p50 180ms and p95 650ms for token latencies at your expected concurrency of 25 streams/region. We'll document experimental load tests.
- Security/compliance: we will include TLS-1.3, mTLS option for private deployments, and a minimal retention config (default 30 days) with the ability to set enterprise retention. Monica will attach our SOC2 summary during procurement.

Technical notes / questions before design freeze:
1) For `order_submit` async callbacks: prefer HTTP POST with idempotency key `x-rd-idempotency` — is that acceptable?
2) Is Carte's callback endpoint able to accept retries with exponential backoff (we'll implement up to 5 retries)?
3) Example event shape (we'll send a preliminary JSON in the drive folder):

{
  "id": "evt_...",
  "ts": "2025-04-15T15:00:00Z",
  "intent": "submit_order",
  "entities": {"medication": "atorvastatin"},
  "confidence": 0.92,
  "tools_called": [ {"tool_name":"order_submit","status":"queued","request_id":"rq_123"} ]
}

I'll bring an editable schema to the call. After the sync we'll update the decision log and push the schema to the drive link. 

Links: HubSpot deal HS-98765, and a placeholder DocuSign we will route through once SOW is approved: https://redwood.app/docusign/RD-98542

See you at 11:00 PT.

--
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.ai

From: Danielle Cho <danielle.cho@cartehealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena@cartehealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Apr 2025 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Decision log + handoff: runtime outputs, streaming & tool-calling

Thanks Camila — that approach works for us. Quick confirmations: 
- We will use `patient_id` + `dob` for reconciliation; no SSNs.
- Callbacks: we accept HTTP POST with `x-rd-idempotency` header and will accept retries.
- 11:00 PT works for the sync.

After the call we'll sign the SOW and confirm a start date for Sprint 0 (target week of 4/21).

Best,

Danielle

--
Danielle Cho
Sr. Platform Engineer, Carte Health
danielle.cho@cartehealth.com

Attachments: none
